details:
Broad arrowheads are often used in Fletching, and are one of the most commonly traded items in the game. Slayer shops sell 21000 of them a day for 50 coins each, and while the stock is shared between most of the shops, Turael and Spria in Burthorpe have an entirely separate stock, so up to 63000 total can be bought per day, from Turael/Spria and one other slayer master. Additionally, Notterazzo in the Wilderness Bandit Camp sells an additional 21000 daily, though this requires being skulled and has the risk of being killed.

The fastest way is to use the Slayer cape perk to quickly teleport to both Slayer masters. If the player doesn't own the cape, teleporting to Burthorpe via the Lodestone Network, then walking north and west to Turael/Spria is a good alternative. After buying the stock there, teleport to Sumona using a ring of slaying, and buy the stock there, then teleport to Edgeville and ask Vala to opt into PVP before running to the Wilderness camp. They can then be banked or sold on the Grand Exchange. Other slayer masters will also work, such as Kuradal (using the ferocious ring or the constructed fairy ring), Mazchna (using the Canifis lodestone), and Duradel/Lapalok (using the karamja gloves 3 teleport). Use the Wilderness sword 4's Edgeville teleport to leave the Wilderness quickly after buying Notterazzo's stock.

Note that the listed activity time is 2 minutes, but it could be much less if part of a larger daily run.

details:
Cactus spines can be picked from the cactus patches in Al Kharid, Menaphos and on anachronia. A new one spawns on the cactus every 25 minutes, for up to 3 total per patch. Use the Al Kharid lodestone and walk east to the cactus patch. Pick the three spines, possibly noting them with the tool leprechaun. Repeat at the Menaphos cactus patch, using the Menaphos lodestone and walking north-west to the patch. If you have totem of the abyss on the northern location you can then use Anachronia Teleport and harvest the anachronia patch.

Completing the hard Desert Tasks is strongly recommended, as it will double the yield of cactus spines. When combined with the giant ent, you'll get an average of 9 spines per patch, up from 3 without any bonuses. 

If possible, you should use a giant ent familiar, which has a 50% chance of doubling the yield of cactus spines, giving you an average of 4.5 spines instead of 3. That makes this method work well with other harvesting money makers, such as picking papayas or coconuts. The 75 minute timer also makes it coincide well with herb farming runs (which can be done every 80 minutes), although giant ents do not give a harvest boost to herbs.

One of these, gold leaves is consistently profitable to buy from him and sell on the Grand Exchange. Purchase the items listed in the Outputs section above with non-zero quantities; those listed at zero quantity are either not profitable or do not have a high enough trade volume to support reliable sales.

The easiest way to get to the Stonemason is using the Luck of the Dwarves teleport, which brings the player just north-east of his shop. Alternatively, use the Keldagrim trapdoor in the north-west corner of the Grand Exchange. The Stonemason's shop is located in the southernmost part of Keldagrim West. Buy all of his limestone bricks — this should take 18 trips to the bank, which is found to the north-west. In the past his other stock has occasionally been profitable, but this is often not the case as those items see little use and can be obtained in small amounts at lower costs - either from the Bandit Duty Free shop in the case of marble blocks and gold leaf, or as a rare reward from Menaphite gift offerings for magic stone.

Once you've collected all the materials you want to buy, you can sell them on the Grand Exchange.

Gerrant's Fishy Business has a stock of 1,000 harpoons that he sells for 45 coins each. The stock replenishes fully every 24 hours. Since harpoons are worth due to them being an ingredient in ibis pouches, buying all of the harpoons from Gerrant's shop and banking at the deposit box next to the Monks of Entrana is a good way to make money in free-to-play daily.

To get to the shop, use the Port Sarim lodestone, which takes you just a few feet away from the building. Go inside and buy 28 harpoons, and then run north-east to the deposit box on the docks. Run back to the shop and repeat. If you are running low on run energy, you could use the lodestone network to teleport from the deposit box to the shop, which takes about the same amount of time as running. If teleporting, make sure to utilise the "previous destination" right-click option on the lodestones. Each run takes about 40-45 seconds, so buying all 1000 harpoons takes about 25 minutes. When finished, re-sell the harpoons on the Grand Exchange.

Players with a Ring of Kinship may also teleport to Daemonheim to bank their harpoons.

Members can also use Harry's Fishing Shop in Catherby for the same purpose, and since it is closer to a bank, buying all 1000 harpoons will only take about 18-20 minutes. However only 300 will restock in 24h and members usually have much better ways to make money (even through other shop arbitrage) so this is not recommended.

There are two locations to brew ales at: upstairs of the Laughing Miner Pub in Eastern Keldagrim and the basement of The Green Ghost inn in Port Phasmatys. Start with the vat in Keldagrim.

Fill your inventory with 2 empty buckets or buckets of water, 2 barley malts, 1 package of "The stuff", 4 clean harralander, two empty pots or pots of ale yeast (there is a pot respawn in Keldagrim), and 2 Calquat kegs. Head to the vat in Eastern Keldagrim via the trapdoor northwest of the Grand Exchange for the quickest access. The Laughing Miner Pub is located north of the mine carts, and northwest of the pub is a well to fill your empty buckets with water if they aren't already filled. Head to the pub and go upstairs to the brewery. Pick up two pots from the pot respawn near the vat if you don't have them already. Talk to Blandebir to fill up your two empty pots with ale yeast for 25 coins each. After you have all the necessary items, fill up the vat by putting in the two buckets of water, two barley malts, The Stuff, four clean harralanders and one pot of ale yeast. You must fill the vat in the correct order - don't forget The Stuff, it increases the chance of mature ale, which is worth more, to 50%. After you put the ale yeast in, the ale will begin to ferment. The vat in Keldagrim can take 8 hours to 2 days to finish fermenting.

Head back to the Grand Exchange via the mine carts, and withdraw the same items once again to fill the vat in Port Phasmatys. Withdraw an Ectophial for the quickest access to the brewery, 2 barley malts, 1 package of "The stuff", 4 clean harralander, and 2 Calquat kegs. You should have 2 empty buckets and 1 pot of ale yeast in your inventory from your earlier trip to Keldagrim. Use your Ectophial and head to The Green Ghost inn, southeast of the Ectofuntus. Go downstairs to the brewery, and use the tap on the far wall to fill up your empty buckets with water. Repeat the vat-filling process by putting in the two buckets of water, two barley malts, The Stuff, four clean harralanders and the last pot of ale yeast, in that order. After you put the ale yeast in, the ale will begin to ferment. The vat in Port Phasmatys takes a minimum of 2 days to ferment, but rarely exceeds that.

When a vat of greenman's ale is done, the examine text will say "This vat is filled with [mature] Greenman's ale." Click the valve on the vat to empty the vat into the nearby barrel, then use your Calquat keg on the barrel to collect the ale. If you check the Port Phasmatys ale two days after it begins fermenting to see if it's done, you can go through the same vat-filling process to collect and refill the ale vats, starting with Keldagrim, in one go.

Potion flasks are popular because they can hold 2 more doses per inventory space over vials. Once daily, you can mine up to 75 red sandstone (or 50 if you have not completed the Elite Desert Tasks) which can be turned into potion flasks.

The first location for red sandstone is just outside of Oo'glog. This location can be mined for 50 sand stone a day and is right near the Robust glass machine. Farming godly grapes and turning them into wine can be very profitable as the wines (mainly Wine of Zamorak and Wine of Saradomin) are used for popular high-level potions. To maximise profit, you should have:
* Magic secateurs from A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, which boost yield 10%

Without these items, godly grape farming is much less profitable. Normal, oak, teak, or mahogany planks may be used to build the vine frame; this guide uses s, as they are currently the cheapest.

Begin your run at Seers' Village with 10 s, 8 godly grapevine seeds, and 2 supercompost. Pick the grapes from the patch, using the leprechaun to note all grapes. When the patch is empty, apply supercompost first, then build a frame with 5 planks, and finally plant the seeds.

Use Watchtower Teleport next, exit the building and go directly east and use the underwall tunnel agility shortcut to cross into Yanille. Repeat the process for harvesting and planting grapes here. Run to the bank and take out 10 more planks, 8 more seeds, and 2 more supercompost.

The next patch should be the Lumbridge patch. Travel here by using the combat bracelet teleport to the Champion's Guild and running south-east, jump over the fence. Harvest the grapevines.

Next you should teleport to Port Sarim (a captain's log is the best option) and take the boat to Entrana. The patch is directly west of where the boat will take you. In case you have any equipment that is not allowed on the boat (like the Farming cape) use the deposit box by the boat. Once there harvest and plant your grapes.

Finally, teleport to any bank and create wine. Grapes can be used on the jugs of water or vice versa. Also, note that wine can ferment in the bank, so you do not need to wait for it to ferment before starting a new inventory.

details:
Make sure you're actually using the alchemiser mk. II, instead of the regular alchemiser. If you do not, the profit gained from this activity will be lower than shown on this page as that machine also requires fire runes and processes fewer items every day. For more detailed information on which item to select, see the Item prices section below.

You will first need to have built a regular alchemiser, then create the alchemiser mk. II. You can build a alchemiser mk. II in the Invention Guild with 108 Invention. If provided with machine charge, this machine will cast the High level Alchemy spell on the provided items. The machine will alchemise 600 items daily. It can hold up to 5,000 items at once, and thus can be left to run just over 8 days without any required input. 

It is possible to boost your Invention level with an extreme invention potion by 17 levels, allowing you to build the alchemiser Mk. II and a jumbo generator at level 91 Invention. Once you have boosted, you must go to the inventor's workbench and research the blueprint.

The buy limit for dragon items is either 10 every four hours (60 per day) or 100 every four hours (600 per day), depending on the item. As the alchemiser mk. II alchemises 600 items per day and you can run 2 at a time. You may need to purchase items directly from other players, buy them while doing other activities, use different item types, or use alternate accounts to bypass the GE buy limits and maximise profits.

Alchable products coming from the common drop table of Zamorakian Undercity such as ascendri bolts (e) and large blunt rune salvage are currently great options for the alchemiser machine. Such items have very high buy limits. Items such as certain dragon items may give greater profit, but a player cannot buy enough to match the rate of the machine.

With a jumbo generator, up to two alchemisers mk. II can be run at a time, potentially resulting in doubled profit, at the expense of being limited in terms of what other machines can be used. To allow profit to be easily calculated for any combination of machines, this page calculates profit on a per-machine basis.

details:
As a tertiary ingredient used in the Summoning skill, marigolds are always in demand. And with Farming being almost the only source of marigolds, the demand is not always met. Farming marigolds can thus be somewhat profitable for low-level players, as it requires only level 2 Farming and is even available to non-members.

Members have access to four farming patches in which marigolds can be farmed - one near Falador, one near Port Phasmatys, one in Catherby and one at the Manor Farm. Only the one near Falador is available to free players, so if you're not a member you'll make roughly one quarter of the profits listed here. Apart from membership, none of these patches have any requirements to access, but the one by Port Phasmatys can be time-consuming to get to without the ectophial or a modified farmer's hat (the latter of which can only be used three times a day) - the easiest way to get there without either of those is teleporting to the Canifis lodestone, though skipping the patch might be a better option. The Falador patch also takes a little bit of time to reach without the Explorer's ring 3 or the South Falador Teleport spell, although the Draynor Village lodestone is reasonably close by. The Manor Farm and Catherby patches are easy to reach with the lodestone Network, and should always be used.

Every five minutes while growing, marigolds have a risk of becoming diseased. When diseased, the marigolds have a roughly 50% risk of dying every 5 minutes and will not grow further unless cured using plant cure. As the frequency of disease isn't known, the profit calculation doesn't include this - actual profit may be somewhat lower than the listed number for this reason. Using compost, supercompost, or ultracompost reduces the risk of this happening, although the cost of the compost may outweight the benefits this involves - this is certainly the case for the rather expensive ultracompost, but might not be for the cheaper compost or supercompost.

To help you keep track of when your marigolds have finished growing, you may want to use an out-of-game timer and/or wear an amulet of farming.

When you expect the marigolds to be fully grown (roughly 20 minutes after planting), head to each of the patches you used and pick the marigolds. If they died, clear the patch instead. If they are alive but diseased, the nearby farmers sell plant cure for 25 coins if you talk to them - you won't get any marigolds this time around, but it saves you a seed. Once you have picked the flowers or cleared the patch, plant another marigold seed. You may want to add compost or supercompost before planting the seed. Then head to the next patch if there are any left, or a bank or the Grand Exchange when you're finished with all the patches.

Buying marigold seeds from the Draynor Seed Market might be cheaper than buying them off the Grand Exchange. The seeds are cheap enough compared to the flowers that this should not make a large difference, however.

details:
Bottled dinosaur roars are used in high level potions (for example vulnerability bombs). Raising rex dinosaurs with the goal of getting these roars can be profitable while also giving a lot of farming experience. With an optimal setup, seven animals can be growing at all time on average, using a single breeding pair in the breeding pen. Higher level dinosaurs give more experience and resources.

The strategy for this method is as follows:

* Go to the Anachronia Dinosaur Farm. It can be reached from a Max Guild garden skilling portal (including through grace of the elves), or the mystical tree upstairs in the Manor Farm.
* Check the large pens and breeding pen. Any animals should be health checked, and any non-breeding elder animals should be removed. Make sure the troughs have enough food to last until your next visit.
* Check the breeding pen. If the large pens have space, move non-breeding animals to large pens.
* If all pens are full, temporarily replace breeding animals with a male and a female adult animals (if possible). It is better to have animals with bad perks breeding than no animals breeding at all. This way, you can have up to 10 animals growing at the same time.
* If space is available again, put the breeding pair back in the breeding pen.
* Sell elder animals (except breeding pair) for beans or to other players.

It is recommended to check once or twice per day to maintain the 7 animal average. Higher level animals grow slower and make maintaining the average easier, but it is feasible to do this with any of the large pen dinosaurs.

Maintaining food in the large pens is not required, but healthy and happy animals give significantly more experience than sick ones. The produce remains the same. Meat can be purchased from the grand exchange or from Fresh Meat after As a First Resort.

Keep an eye out for animals with the traits 'Young at Heart' and 'Old at Heart', which will alter by 25% how slowly any animals possessing these traits will age. Young at Heart animals age 25% slower than normal. Old at Heart animals age 25% faster.

The inputs above are an example and may vary significantly with the boss chosen and/or your levels and prowess.

Completing Soul Reaper tasks from Death is a very profitable weekly, as each completed task rewards reaper points which are valued at . The profit listed above is purely from purchasing an incomplete hydrix once you have 300 reaper points. The drops from the bosses will increase the profit further.

Each task awards between 7 and 39 reaper points, with the higher values obtained from completing the highest tier pvm content in the game. However since there is no limit to the number of reaper tasks that players can complete, maximising points gained does not require completing the hardest pvm content. There is a limit of 300 reaper points that can be earned per week, so it does not strictly matter which bosses you kill. To minimise the amount of time required to obtain 300 reaper points:
* Enable group tasks for soul reaper, as this gives 25% increased points for all tasks
* Disable extended tasks, as this makes each task take twice as long for only 25% increased points
* Bring a Grim gem while completing the task, to obtain a following task without having to return to Death's office
* If given Reaper's choice, it is often faster overall to choose a mid level boss (relative to the player's skill level) with a task that can be completed in a few minutes, rather than a higher level boss that might take significantly longer for a relatively small increase in points.

Reaching higher tiers of Combat Mastery gives you an increasing chance of 'Reaper's Choice', where you get to choose the boss for your task, maxing out at 100%. This allows you player to focus on only the bosses you want to kill; otherwise, you can spend 30 slayer points to reroll a task.

With 100% chance of reapers choice, the fastest method to reach 300 reaper points is to complete the Dagannoth Kings soul reaper task 17 times, which requires an average of 170 kills. This is due to the fact that dagannoth kings have low health, so can be killed quickly, and one can be killed while the other 2 are respawning. As an alternative, the Chaos Elemental soul reaper task can be completed 38 times, for an average of 171 kills, but more time will be spent waiting for it to respawn.
